title: Quality scorers and eval suite for quantized model profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a modular, testable quality-scoring framework and end-to-end eval suite that validates FP8/INT8 quantization profiles against our production-quality bar. This ticket covers scorer adapters (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, ROUGE/BLEU, task-specific F1/RR), result aggregation, storage of artifacts into the eval bucket, and CI gating for calibration runs. The goal is to enable repeatable, per-profile quality assertions that can be run in CI, on-demand from the console, or as part of the calibration workflow.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scorer framework implemented with pluggable adapters for perplexity, sacreBLEU, ROUGE-L, MMLU-style multi-task accuracy, and a generic task-scorer interface; 2) End-to-end pipeline stores JSON artifacts (per-input scores, aggregated metrics, confidence intervals) in s3://redwood-evals/quant-profiles/{profile}/{date}; 3) Baseline comparison harness runs automatically for FP32 vs INT8 vs FP8 for a given profile and outputs human-readable report; 4) CI gate that fails if selected profile degrades beyond per-task thresholds; 5) Dashboards surfaced in Console linking to raw artifacts and evaluation summaries.
metrics_spec: task-specific F1 and exact-match for QA/NER
test_plan:
- Add unit tests for each scorer adapter (mocked model outputs)
- Integration test: run harness on small curated eval set under FP32/INT8/FP8 quantized checkpoints and assert metric deltas are within thresholds
- Performance smoke: measure scorer runtime and ensure end-to-end eval of 5k examples completes within 45m on CI runner; add batching where needed
- CI gating: synthetic quick-run (50 samples) required for each calibration PR; full run nightly and on-demand via Console
- Store all artifacts and link in PR for reviewers
implementation_notes:
Design choices and trade-offs considered:
- Use sacrebleu for deterministic BLEU scores to avoid tokenization drift across languages.
- Use public rouge implementation that supports tokenization normalization used in our training pipelines to ensure apples-to-apples.
- Perplexity computed on tokenized logits after aligning tokenizer vocab; note FP8/INT8 may introduce logit floor/clipping — we apply tiny additive smoothing to avoid -inf.
- MMLU-style suites run as grouped binary correctness tasks; we compute macro and micro averages and also per-subject breakdowns to catch regressed capabilities.
- Sampling vs greedy generation: deterministically evaluate by using greedy/beam for metric stability; expose sampling-based evaluation separately for diversity checks.
- Keep scorer implementations side-effect free and pure functions to facilitate local developer testing and reproducibility.
- Store raw generations and logits for a small subset (privacy-scrubbed) to enable downstream error analysis; use KMS-encrypted storage for any PII-containing artifacts.
